# hooks/settle-meter Specification

## Purpose

Shows a `/interlock:settle --review` run while it runs: a status line naming the change, the pull request and the last thing the CLI printed, and a pane grouping the run by the settle skill's sections and rounds as a timeline, with each spawn attributed to its role, drawn by the same hooks module as the ship meter and the spec meter from what crossed the Bash, Skill and Agent tools, and deciding nothing.

## Requirements

### Requirement: The settle meter SHALL go live on every load of the plugin's settle skill in an interactive session, SHALL record whether `--review` was passed, and SHALL take the change, the pull request and the head from the CLI's lines alone

The module SHALL start a settle run when the plugin's settle skill is loaded in a session whose start reported it interactive, with or without `--review`: a prompt whose first word is `/interlock:settle`, or a Skill call naming `interlock:settle` the engine did not mark errored. The run SHALL record whether its arguments contain the word `--review`, and whether they contain the word `--create`. The change, pull request and head SHALL be read only as the earlier rules read them.

Of the prompt and the Skill call, only the first word and the presence of the words `--review` and `--create` SHALL be read, and both SHALL be passed on exactly as they came. A Skill call naming `interlock:review-code` while a settle run is live SHALL change no section: it lands in the section already open. At the start the status line and the pane SHALL read `change: unknown until named`. The change name SHALL be taken only from the CLI's own argv (`--change <name>` on the settle lines, the positional change on `interlock settle conformance-brief`, `interlock merge-confidence` and `interlock domain-context`, `--metrics <name>` on `interlock review`) or a `change` field in a result's JSON; the pull request number only from `--pr <n>`, a `pr` field, or the positional number on a `gh pr` stage; the head only from `--head <sha>` or a `head` or `head.sha` field. None of them SHALL be taken from a file path, a prompt or a tool input. A second settle load in the same session SHALL start the record over, with its own `--review` reading, and say so once on the debug log. In a non-interactive session every hook this requirement adds SHALL return at its first line.

#### Scenario: Happy path — a load with `--review` starts the run and the brief names the pass

- **GIVEN** an interactive session
- **WHEN** the prompt `/interlock:settle --create --review` is submitted
- **THEN** the status line reads `interlock settle: change: unknown until named`, the pane is opened unasked, it reads `with --review` beneath its header, and the prompt reaches the engine unchanged
- **AND** when `interlock settle remediate-brief --review .claude/ship/settle/review-r0.json --round 1 --change route-prose-spawns-by-role --head a96cb82cedb626d9b6c11c1f6a090b7e52a2afa8 --pr 25 … --json` resolves, the header names `route-prose-spawns-by-role`, `PR #25` and `head a96cb82`

#### Scenario: Happy path — a load without `--review` starts the run and groups its pass under `resolve`

- **GIVEN** an interactive session
- **WHEN** the prompt `/interlock:settle --create` is submitted, then `interlock changes` exits 0, then `interlock pipeline …` and `interlock merge-confidence <change> … --json` resolve with `verdict: 'MERGE', score: 91`, then `gh pr edit 25 --add-label …` and `interlock drift --changed … --json` resolve
- **THEN** the pane opens unasked and reads `without --review` beneath its header, and draws the groups `resolve`, `merge confidence`, `publish` and `drift` in that order, with no `review` and no `round <n>` group
- **AND** the run ends at the drift line, and the status line reads `interlock settle <change> #25: merge confidence · MERGE 91`

#### Scenario: Failure — a non-interactive session draws nothing

- **GIVEN** `session.start` reporting `isInteractive: false`
- **WHEN** `/interlock:settle --review` or `/interlock:settle --create` is submitted and the settle lines, spawns and turn events of a pass follow
- **THEN** no status line is set, no pane is opened, no toast is shown and no record is kept
- **AND** every hook resolved to what the engine alone would have done

#### Scenario: Edge case — the review-code skill alone, and a second settle load

- **GIVEN** an interactive session in which the settle skill was not loaded
- **WHEN** a Skill call names `interlock:review-code` and four `general-purpose` agents whose prompts begin `# Dimension: ` are spawned
- **THEN** no status line is set and the pane reads that no settle run is live in this session
- **AND** when a live settle run loaded with `--review` exists and `/interlock:settle` is submitted again without it, the record starts over with `change: unknown until named`, reads `without --review`, the earlier rows are not kept, and one debug-log line says a new settle run replaced the previous one

### Requirement: The status line and the pane SHALL repeat the CLI's own words from the settle and review lines, read at every pipe stage, and SHALL make no verdict of their own

While a settle run is live, a Bash call of the main session (one whose event carries no `agentId`: every keyed line of a pass runs there, and a ship lane's `interlock verify exec` or `git commit` is never the pass's) whose command, or one of its segments or pipe stages, begins with one of the keyed lines SHALL be let through and its result read, on the Bash hook's path with no ship run live and on its path with one live alike, and whether or not the spec meter's reader keyed or declined the same line. Segments are split at unquoted `&&`, `||`, `;` or line breaks; each segment is further split at unquoted `|` and at `$(`, a `$(` inside double quotes included; the body of a quoted heredoc is one argument and is never re-split; and every stage is keyed by its own first words. A line that crosses again SHALL append a row, never replace the earlier one.

The keyed lines and the fields read from each:
- `gh pr view` / `glab mr view` naming no pull request of its own (the branch's lookup: no number or `<n>` follows `view`): the command words and the exit code
- `interlock routing --json` (with or without `--depth`): `depth`, `roles.<role>.model`, `roles.<role>.effort`, `review.dimensions`, `review.skeptics`, `banners`; `interlock routing <role> --json`: `role`, `model`, `effort`, `banners`
- `interlock surface`, `interlock domain-context`, `interlock gate`, `interlock changes`, `interlock review-policy`, `interlock autonomy record`, `interlock note derive`: the command words and the exit code
- `interlock review … --json` (with or without `--out <file>`): `counts.raised`, `counts.dismissed`, `counts.surviving`, `counts.carried`, `dimensionStats` by name, `head`, `dimensions.ran`, `dimensions.skipped` (the `name` of each `{ name, reason }`), `dimensions.unavailable`, `dimensions.depth`, the skipped and unavailable names drawn on the review row; never `dimensions.completed`
- `interlock settle comment --round <n> --head <sha>`, `interlock settle replies --head <sha>`: the command words, the round and the exit code; the `gh pr comment <n>` / `glab mr note <iid>` stage beside them: its pull request number only
- `interlock settle tree-check`: the stdout it printed — `clean`, `clean (tolerated: …)`, or `dirty (<k>):` and the paths it listed — and the exit code
- `interlock settle test-paths … --json`: `protected` and `unprotected` by count and the `protected` paths, or, when `profile` is null, the `reason` field verbatim; with `--protected-only`, the exit code
- `interlock settle remediate-brief … --round <r> --change <c> --head <sha> --pr <n> … --json`: `findings` and `deferred` by count, `reReviewDimensions`; on exit 1 the stderr line beginning `STOP: `, verbatim, which ends the loop on the pane
- `interlock settle fixer-result --round <r>`: the stdout line `round <r>: <a> fixed, <b> not fixed`
- `git commit -m "<message>"`: the message's first line, or `(message not read)` when the message is written inside `$( )`; `git push`: the exit code; both only inside a round, and passed through unread outside one
- `gh pr ready <n>` / `glab mr update <iid> --ready`: the exit code
- `interlock settle conformance-brief <c> --head <sha>`: the exit code, and on an empty stdout the stderr line, verbatim
- `interlock verify plan`, `interlock verify exec --kind <kind>`, `interlock verify judge`, `interlock verify coverage`: the kind and the exit code; a result with no stdout reads `result not seen (redirected)`
- `gh pr checks <n> --watch` / `glab ci get --merge-request <iid>` when it is not piped onward (piped into `interlock pipeline` it is that line's input): `background` when the call ran in the background, else the exit code
- `interlock pipeline`: the stdout line beginning `pipeline <sha>:` or `pending <sha>:`, verbatim
- `interlock merge-confidence <c> … --json`: `verdict`, `score`, `head.sha`, and `labels.verdict.name` and `labels.score.name` drawn as `labels <verdict name>, <score name>`; with `--markdown` or a redirected result, the exit code, as a row of its own after the verdict row
- `interlock merge-confidence --label-names --json`: `labels.verdictNames` and `labels.scorePrefix`, as a row of its own, never `(unparsed)` for want of a verdict
- `gh pr edit <n> --add-label <names>` / `glab mr update <iid> --label <names>`: the label names; `gh pr edit <n> --remove-label <names>` / `glab mr update <iid> --unlabel <names>`: `removed` and the label names
- `interlock drift --changed … --json`: `unarchived` and `stale.broken` by count

Reading rules: stages SHALL be applied in the command's order; a stage whose result does not parse as JSON, or lacks the fields the line names, SHALL be shown as that line with `(unparsed)` and its first line of text, never as a verdict, and SHALL leave one debug-log line; a result the engine kept out of line (too large to read inline) SHALL be shown as `result not seen (too large)`, and a review record's `--out review-r<n>.json` SHALL still name its round; a stage's exit code SHALL be drawn as `exit <n>` only when the call's exit is that stage's own — the stage runs outside every `$( )`, is the last stage of its pipeline, sits in the command's last `;`-separated list, and that list joins its pipelines with `&&` alone, with more than one pipeline only for an exit of 0 — and otherwise as `exit not its own`; a failed `git commit … && git push` SHALL read `exit <n> from the commit or the push`; control characters SHALL be made spaces and every row, status line and toast cut to `settle row chars` from `interlock limits`; every other Bash call SHALL be passed through at the first line, its result unread. The module SHALL compare no count against any threshold, SHALL draw no tick, cross or verdict word of its own, and SHALL show no `quiet <n> min`.

#### Scenario: Happy path — the PR #25 pass reads back in the CLI's words

- **GIVEN** a live settle run
- **WHEN** `interlock review … --metrics route-prose-spawns-by-role --dimensions … --head a96cb82… --out .claude/ship/settle/review-r0.json --json` resolves with `counts: { raised: 6, dismissed: 0, surviving: 6 }` and `dimensions.depth: 'lean'`, then `interlock settle fixer-result --round 1 …` resolves with `round 1: 1 fixed, 0 not fixed`, then `gh pr view 25 --json headRefOid,statusCheckRollup | interlock pipeline --github - --required "test" --out .claude/ship/pipeline.json` resolves with `pipeline 161f955…: 3 check(s) (3 pass, 0 fail, 0 pending, 0 skipped); required: test; excluded: none`
- **THEN** the review row reads `6 raised · 0 dismissed · 6 surviving · head a96cb82`, the header reads `lean`, round 1's result row reads `round 1: 1 fixed, 0 not fixed`, and the merge-confidence group's first row is the pipeline line verbatim
- **AND** the status line after the last of them reads `interlock settle route-prose-spawns-by-role #25: merge confidence · pipeline 161f955`

#### Scenario: Failure — a STOP line, a redirected judge and an unparsed result

- **GIVEN** a live settle run in round 2
- **WHEN** `interlock settle remediate-brief … --round 2 … --json` exits 1 with stderr `interlock: STOP: round 2 is the verdict round (remediationRounds=2; no fix round remains)` and nothing on stdout, then `interlock verify judge --plan … --results … --context final --head 161f955… --json > .claude/ship/settle/verify.json.tmp` exits 0 with no stdout, then `interlock merge-confidence route-prose-spawns-by-role … --json` resolves with text that is not JSON
- **THEN** round 2's row reads `STOP: round 2 is the verdict round (remediationRounds=2; no fix round remains)`, the verify row reads `judge exit 0 · result not seen (redirected)`, and the merge-confidence row reads `merge-confidence (unparsed)` with the result's first line
- **AND** no row reads halted, passed, failed or any word the CLI did not print, and one debug-log line names the unparsed line
- **AND** in a pass whose round 1 `git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=all | interlock settle tree-check --change route-prose-spawns-by-role --status -` exits 1 with stdout `dirty (1):` and `  notes.txt`, round 1's row reads `tree-check dirty (1): notes.txt · exit 1`

#### Scenario: Edge case — pipe stages, a background watch and a compound command

- **GIVEN** a live settle run
- **WHEN** `git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=all | interlock settle tree-check --change route-prose-spawns-by-role --status -` resolves with `clean`, then `interlock settle comment --review .claude/ship/settle/review-r0.json --head a96cb82… --round 0 | gh pr comment 25 --body-file -` resolves with a comment URL, then `gh pr checks 25 --watch` is called with `run_in_background: true`, then `git commit -m "fix(review): answer the PR #25 review round 1" -m "Refs: #25" && git push` resolves
- **THEN** the pane reads `tree-check clean · exit 0`, the comment row reads `round 0 · exit 0` with `PR #25` taken from the second stage, the checks row reads `gh pr checks 25 --watch · background`, and round 1 reads `commit fix(review): answer the PR #25 review round 1 · push exit 0`
- **AND** `glab mr note 7 --message "$(interlock settle comment --review .claude/ship/settle/review-r0.json --head a96cb82… --round 0)"` is read as a comment row too, its `interlock` stage split from inside the double quotes, and every one of those calls reached the engine unchanged

### Requirement: Each spawn of a live settle run SHALL be attributed from the prompt's first line against pinned sources, and its model and effort SHALL be shown by source and labelled

While a settle run is live, the module SHALL read each `agent.spawn` as it crosses and pass it on unchanged. The role SHALL be read from the prompt's lines, each match anchored at a line's start and covering the whole source sentence. The prompt's first non-blank line SHALL be tested first against the two CLI-printed sources, which win over every other: `Fix round <r> for change "<c>", … at head <sha>.` is round r's fixer; `Confirm change "<c>" against its diff at head <sha>.` is the conformance worker. Otherwise the lines SHALL be read from the top, and the scan SHALL stop at the first line that is one of: `# Dimension: <words>`, a dimension reviewer named by those words; `You are a skeptical code reviewer.`, the refuting skeptic; `You are an independent reviewer giving a second opinion.`, the second-opinion skeptic. So a repository review policy block prepended to a reviewer's instructions does not hide its role, and a finding quoted inside a fixer's brief never makes it a skeptic. A line copied with a blockquote's `> ` marker SHALL be read without it. A spec run's Explore investigator SHALL be the spec run's and never a settle agent. A prompt with no such line SHALL be drawn as `<subagentType> · unattributed`; the Agent call's `description` SHALL never be drawn. Each agent row SHALL carry: the model requested (the spawn input's `model`, or `inherit` when absent), the model resolved (the spawn result's `model`), the models served (`usage.model` of its steps, distinct), the effort the CLI routed for its role, labelled `routed`, read from the `interlock routing` lines of the pass, reading `routed: not read` once a routing line for the role crossed and could not be read and `routed: not seen` before one has crossed, the engine's per-step `effort` labelled `step` (the latest, and `<first> → <latest>` when they differ), its requests and token counts from its `turn.step` results, its elapsed time from the clock and its `turn.complete` `durationMs`, and the host's `reason` word at its end. Figures SHALL be labelled live until the agent's turn ends. The ship meter's agent records SHALL be untouched by a settle run: a settle agent's steps and turn end SHALL never be tallied as a ship lane, even while a ship run is live.

#### Scenario: Happy path — a dimension reviewer and the fixer are attributed and labelled

- **GIVEN** a live settle run in which `interlock routing --json` resolved with `roles.review-dimension: { model: 'sonnet', effort: 'medium' }` and `interlock routing settle-fixer --json` resolved with `model: null, effort: 'xhigh'`
- **WHEN** an agent is spawned with `subagentType: 'general-purpose'`, `model: 'sonnet'` and a prompt beginning `# Dimension: language & framework`, the engine resolves it `model: 'claude-sonnet-5-5'`, its `turn.step` inputs carry `effort: 'medium'` and its results carry usage, and later an agent is spawned with no `model`, `parentModel: 'claude-opus-5-5'` and a prompt beginning `Fix round 1 for change "route-prose-spawns-by-role", pull request #25, at head a96cb82…`
- **THEN** the review group's dimensions row reads `routed sonnet · medium` and the reviewer's row reads `language & framework · sonnet → claude-sonnet-5-5 · step medium · <n> req · <tokens> · <elapsed> · live`
- **AND** round 1's fixer row reads `fixer · inherit → claude-opus-5-5 · routed — · xhigh · step <level> · … · live`, and when its `turn.complete` carries `reason: 'answer'` and `durationMs: 645000` the row ends `10m 45s · answer`

#### Scenario: Failure — a spawn matching no source, and a spawn before any routing line

- **GIVEN** a live settle run in which no `interlock routing` line has crossed
- **WHEN** an agent is spawned with `subagentType: 'general-purpose'` and a prompt beginning `Please summarise the diff`, then an agent whose prompt begins `You are a skeptical code reviewer.`
- **THEN** the first row reads `general-purpose · unattributed` with its engine figures and no word of its description, and the skeptics row reads `routed: not seen`
- **AND** both spawn calls reached the engine unchanged and the ship meter's agent records are empty

#### Scenario: Edge case — a changed step level, an aborted worker, and a ship run's agents

- **GIVEN** a live settle run in the conformance group
- **WHEN** the conformance worker's first `turn.step` carries `effort: 'medium'` and its latest `effort: 'high'`, and its `turn.complete` carries `reason: 'aborted'`
- **THEN** its row reads `step medium → high` and ends `aborted`, and one toast reads `conformance: aborted`
- **AND** when no settle run is live and a ship run is, the same events change the ship meter's records alone and nothing in the settle record

#### Scenario: Edge case — each role carries its own routed figure, and a policy block precedes a brief

- **GIVEN** a live settle run in which `interlock routing --json` resolved with `roles.review-dimension: { model: 'sonnet', effort: 'medium' }` and `roles.review-skeptic: { model: null, effort: 'xhigh' }`, and `interlock routing settle-conformance --json` resolved with `model: 'sonnet', effort: null`
- **WHEN** an agent is spawned whose prompt begins with a `REPOSITORY REVIEW POLICY` block followed by `# Dimension: technical lead`, then an agent whose prompt begins `You are a skeptical code reviewer.`, then, in the conformance group, an agent whose prompt begins `Confirm change "route-prose-spawns-by-role" against its diff at head 161f955….`
- **THEN** the first is drawn as the `technical lead` dimension reviewer and the dimensions row reads `routed sonnet · medium`, the skeptics row in the same group reads `routed — · xhigh`, and the conformance worker's row reads `routed sonnet · —`
- **AND** no row's routed figure is taken from another role's routing entry

### Requirement: The pane SHALL group the run by the settle skill's sections and rounds as a timeline on both surfaces, and SHALL toast only the CLI's STOP line, the verdict, a turn's non-answer end and a declined placement

The pane SHALL be registered as `interlock-settle` with the command `/interlock-settle` at any width, opened unasked when a settle run starts, and drawn by field on the terminal and desktop surfaces from the same keyed lines: a header (`interlock settle — <change> · PR #<n> · <depth> · head <sha7> · <elapsed>`), then one group per section word of the settle skill in the order the pass runs them — `review` (or `resolve` in a pass loaded without `--review`), `round <n>` for each round seen, `ready`, `conformance`, `verify`, `checks`, `merge confidence`, `publish`, `drift` — each with the clock time it opened, the clock time of its last line and the span between them, its agent rows grouped by role (dimensions, skeptics, fixer, worker) with `<k> spawned · <m> <reason>` counts, the dimensions row drawing the routing listing and the engine's count as two labelled facts (`review dimensions <names> · <k> spawned`), and its CLI rows with their clock times; then a banners area repeating the routing lines' banners verbatim or reading `none`. A group not yet reached SHALL not be drawn; a group the pass skipped SHALL not be invented. Below `settle pane full width (columns)` from `interlock limits` an agent row SHALL keep its role, served model, elapsed time and reason. A row, a group heading or the header the clock could not time SHALL read `time unknown` where its time would be. The pane SHALL raise a toast only for: a `STOP: ` line (its text verbatim), a merge-confidence verdict (`merge-confidence: <verdict> <score>`), a settle agent's turn ending with a reason other than `answer` (`<role>: <reason>`), and an unasked open the surface declined (`/interlock-settle opens the settle meter`). With no settle run live the pane SHALL read that no settle run is live in this session.

The record SHALL hold one open section, and a line SHALL either open a section or append to the one open. Sections SHALL only move forward in the order below; a line whose kind opens an earlier section SHALL append to the section already open.

| section | opened by | also appends here while it is open |
|---------|-----------|------------------------------------|
| `review` | the run's first keyed line, Skill load or spawn | review-code's lines, `interlock review --out …review-r0.json`, `interlock settle comment --round 0`, dimension and skeptic spawns |
| `resolve` | in a pass loaded without `--review`, the run's first keyed line that has no section of its own, in place of `review` | every later line with no section of its own, until a later section opens |
| `round <r>` | `interlock settle tree-check` after `review-r<r-1>.json` has crossed, or `interlock settle remediate-brief --round <r>` when no such tree-check did | the brief, `interlock routing settle-fixer`, the fixer spawn, `fixer-result`, `test-paths`, `git commit`, `git push`, the nested review-code load, its lines and its dimension and skeptic spawns, `interlock review --out …review-r<r>.json`, `interlock settle replies` |
| `ready` | `gh pr ready <n>` / `glab mr update <iid> --ready` | — |
| `conformance` | `interlock settle conformance-brief`, `interlock routing settle-conformance` | the conformance worker's spawn |
| `verify` | `interlock verify plan`, `exec`, `judge`, `coverage` | — |
| `checks` | `gh pr checks <n> --watch` / `glab ci get --merge-request <iid>` | — |
| `merge confidence` | `interlock pipeline`, `interlock merge-confidence <c> … --json` or `--markdown` | — |
| `publish` | a label add or remove line, `interlock merge-confidence --label-names` | any later `merge-confidence` row |
| `drift` | `interlock drift --changed` | — |

In a pass loaded without `--review`, `review` and `round <n>` SHALL never be opened, and every line that would have opened `review` opens or appends to `resolve` instead. A line with no round of its own (the branch's pull request lookup, `surface`, `domain-context`, `routing`, `gate`, `test-paths`, a `tree-check` before any review record, the nested review-code Skill load) and an unattributed spawn SHALL append to the section open.

#### Scenario: Happy path — the pass reads as a grouped timeline on both surfaces

- **GIVEN** a settle run in which the review lines, two rounds, the conformance brief, the verify lines, the pipeline line, `interlock merge-confidence … --json` resolving with `verdict: 'HUMAN', score: 58, head: { sha: '161f955…' }` and then the same command with `--markdown` in place of `--json` exiting 0 have crossed
- **WHEN** the pane is drawn on the terminal and on the desktop
- **THEN** both draw the groups `review`, `round 1`, `round 2`, `conformance`, `verify`, `checks`, `merge confidence` in that order, each with its open time, last time and span, the review group with a dimensions row, a skeptics row, the review record row and the comment row, round 1 with tree-check, brief, fixer, result, commit, re-review and replies rows, round 2 with its tree-check and STOP rows, and the merge-confidence group with the pipeline row, the verdict row `HUMAN 58 · head 161f955` and after it the row `merge-confidence --markdown · exit 0`
- **AND** one toast read `merge-confidence: HUMAN 58`, and the status line reads `interlock settle route-prose-spawns-by-role #25: merge confidence · HUMAN 58`

#### Scenario: Edge case — a re-review's fan-out lands in its round, not in review

- **GIVEN** a live settle run whose review group drew four dimension spawns and the `review-r0.json` record, and in which round 1's `tree-check` and `interlock settle remediate-brief --round 1 …` have crossed
- **WHEN** a Skill call names `interlock:review-code`, then `interlock routing --json` resolves, then an agent whose prompt begins `# Dimension: blast-radius` is spawned, then `interlock review … --out .claude/ship/settle/review-r1.json --json` resolves
- **THEN** the dimension agent, the routing row and the review record are drawn in round 1 as its re-review, and the review group still shows four dimension spawns
- **AND** the status line reads `round 1 · …` throughout and never `review · …`

#### Scenario: Failure — the unasked open is declined, and the command answers with no run

- **GIVEN** an interactive session whose surface answers `isPlaced: false` to an unasked open
- **WHEN** `/interlock:settle --review` is submitted
- **THEN** one toast reads `/interlock-settle opens the settle meter` and the status line is still set
- **AND** when `/interlock-settle` is run in a session with no settle run, the pane opens and reads that no settle run is live in this session, and the command replies with an empty result

#### Scenario: Edge case — a narrow terminal, a skipped group and a running fixer

- **GIVEN** a live settle run in round 1 whose fixer has stepped 18 times over 6m 10s and not ended
- **WHEN** the pane is drawn at 90 columns
- **THEN** the fixer row reads `fixer · claude-opus-5-5 · 6m 10s · live` and the status line reads `interlock settle route-prose-spawns-by-role #25: round 1 · fixer 6m 10s · 18 req`
- **AND** no `ready` group is drawn because no `gh pr ready` or `glab mr update --ready` line crossed, and no row reads any word the CLI, the engine or the clock did not supply

### Requirement: The settle pane SHALL be drawn as bordered cards with toned words from fields beside unchanged row texts, and SHALL highlight the merge-confidence verdict by the CLI's own word

Each pane line SHALL keep the text it reads today, and SHALL carry beside it its kind, its section, coloured spans whose concatenation is exactly the text, and, on a verdict row, the verdict word. A span's tone SHALL only name what a word the CLI, the engine or the clock supplied means. The module SHALL draw single-border cards from those fields alone, never by parsing a text.

The pane SHALL draw, at or above the settle card floor (`settle pane card width (columns)` from `interlock limits`, the width at which a folded agent row keeps its reason inside a card):
- a header card whose border takes the accent colour, holding the header line and the `with --review` or `without --review` line
- one card per section in the order it opened, its border in the current colour while that section is the open one of a live run and dim otherwise, its heading's section word bold in the accent colour and its times dim
- CLI rows with their clock dim; `exit 0` in the ok colour; any other own exit, a `STOP: ` line and the word `(unparsed)` in the alarm colour; `exit not its own` and `result not seen` dim
- role rows indented under their section, and each agent's row indented beneath its role, its name in the name colour and its end word coloured as the ship meter colours a turn word; an agent row wider than the pane SHALL be cut in its middle, so its name and its end word stay, and every other row at its end
- the merge-confidence verdict row inside a card of its own within its section, whose border and verdict word take the verdict's tone: `MERGE` the ok colour, `HUMAN` the warn colour, `BLOCK` the alarm colour; a verdict word outside those three SHALL be drawn uncoloured
- the banners in the warn colour

Indentation SHALL be layout, never characters in a text. Below the settle card floor, or with no width reported, the same lines SHALL be drawn flat with no border. With no settle run live the pane SHALL draw its one no-run text and nothing else. The pane SHALL use only `borderStyle: 'single'`, theme keys and the element props the ship meter already draws with, and SHALL add no tick, cross, glyph or word of its own.

#### Scenario: Happy path — the PR #25 pass draws as cards and the verdict stands out

- **GIVEN** a done settle run whose groups are `review`, `round 1`, `round 2`, `conformance`, `verify`, `checks`, `merge confidence`, whose verdict row reads `HUMAN 58 · head 161f955` and whose round 2 carries a `STOP: ` row
- **WHEN** the pane is drawn at 144 columns on the terminal and on the desktop
- **THEN** each group is one single-border card with a dim border, the header card's border is the accent colour, and the verdict row sits in its own card whose border and the word `HUMAN` take the warn colour
- **AND** the keyed rows read, in order, exactly the texts the pane drew before this change, and every line's spans join to its text

#### Scenario: Edge case — the open round's card is marked while the run is live

- **GIVEN** a live settle run in round 1 whose fixer is running
- **WHEN** the pane is drawn
- **THEN** round 1's card border takes the current colour, the review card's border is dim, the fixer's row is indented beneath the round's rows and its end word `live` takes the colour of a running turn
- **AND** once the drift line ends the run, no card's border takes the current colour

#### Scenario: Failure — a narrow pane draws flat, and an unknown verdict stays uncoloured

- **GIVEN** a done settle run whose verdict row's word is one the meter does not know
- **WHEN** the pane is drawn at 40 columns, and then at 144 columns
- **THEN** at 40 columns no Box has a border and every keyed row still reads its text
- **AND** at 144 columns the verdict card is drawn with a dim border and its word uncoloured, and no pane text contains a tick, a cross, `passed`, `failed` or `halted` that the CLI did not print

### Requirement: The settle run SHALL end at the drift line, start over on a second load, and reset at the session boundary, and the module's one status line SHALL rank a live run above a finished one

When `interlock drift --changed … --json` crosses a live settle run, the run SHALL move to `done`. In a run loaded without `--create`, the branch's pull request lookup exiting other than 0, as its own exit, SHALL move it to `done` too, since the settle skill stops there and nothing else would end the run; with `--create`, or with an exit that is not the stage's own, it SHALL change nothing. An `interlock drift` line without `--changed`, as the spec flow runs it, SHALL change nothing: the pane SHALL keep its rows, with the time the run ended, and a later keyed line SHALL change nothing and be named once on the debug log. A labels line (`gh pr edit <n> --add-label …`, `glab mr update <iid> --label …`) SHALL be a `publish` row and SHALL NOT end the run. The `publish` and `drift` sections SHALL NOT retarget the status line: from the merge-confidence section on, it SHALL keep that section's last words, and `done` SHALL keep them until the boundary. The status figure SHALL otherwise be the open section's last CLI words or, while one or more attributed agents of the section run, the longest-running one's role, elapsed time and requests, preceded by `<k> live` when more than one runs; an unattributed spawn SHALL never take the figure. At a classic session-start event whose source is `clear`, `resume` or `fork` the settle run SHALL reset in the same hook and on the same event as the ship and spec runs, the status line cleared and the pane redrawn to its no-run text; a source of `startup` or `compact` SHALL leave it as it is. Only a session that held a settle run SHALL name the first keyed line after the boundary or the drift line, once; after that, and in a session that never ran settle, a Bash call SHALL not be parsed for a settle line at all. A Workflow tool call the launch rule recognises as an accepted ship launch SHALL leave the settle record and pane as they are and SHALL take the status line at the launch itself; while that ship run is live the status line SHALL read the ship position and never both, and after it closes or halts the line falls back through the order below. The module SHALL compose its one status line in one place, a live run ranking above a finished one: the ship position while a ship run is live, otherwise the spec line while a spec run is live, otherwise the settle line while a settle run is live, otherwise the spec line while a spec run is stopped at its checkpoint, otherwise the settle line while a settle run is done, otherwise nothing.

#### Scenario: Happy path — the drift line ends the run and the verdict stays on the line

- **GIVEN** a live settle run whose merge-confidence row reads `HUMAN 58`
- **WHEN** `gh pr edit 25 --add-label "interlock/human-review,interlock/score-58"` resolves and then `interlock drift --changed … --json` resolves with `unarchived: ['route-prose-spawns-by-role']` and `stale.broken: []`
- **THEN** the run is still live after the labels line, the publish row reads `labels interlock/human-review, interlock/score-58`, the drift row reads `unarchived 1 · broken 0`, the pane reads `done <ISO>`, and the status line reads `interlock settle route-prose-spawns-by-role #25: merge confidence · HUMAN 58` throughout and is not cleared
- **AND** a later `interlock settle fixer-result …` changes nothing and is named once on the debug log

#### Scenario: Edge case — a load on a branch with no pull request ends at the failed lookup

- **GIVEN** an interactive session whose spec run is stopped at its checkpoint
- **WHEN** `/interlock:settle` is submitted, then `gh pr view 2>/dev/null` exits 1, then an agent whose prompt begins `# Dimension: ` is spawned, the review-code skill is loaded and `interlock routing --json` resolves
- **THEN** the pane reads `without --review`, its `resolve` group holds `gh pr view exit 1`, it reads `done <ISO>`, and the spawn, the load and the routing line are not drawn
- **AND** the status line reads the spec run's checkpoint line from the lookup on; with `/interlock:settle --create` the same lookup leaves the run live

#### Scenario: Failure — a ship launch during a settle run takes the line and leaves the pane

- **GIVEN** a live settle run with its status line set
- **WHEN** a Workflow call naming `workflows/ship.js` returns `status: 'async_launched'` with a run id, and after it `interlock settle fixer-result --round 1 …` resolves with `round 1: 1 fixed, 0 not fixed`
- **THEN** the status line reads the ship meter's `interlock: <change> …` form and never both, the settle pane still draws its groups and agents, and round 1's result row reads `round 1: 1 fixed, 0 not fixed`
- **AND** when the launch returns an error or a deny, the settle line stays

#### Scenario: Edge case — a clear, a compaction, and a spec run beside a settle run

- **GIVEN** a live settle run with a status line set and groups drawn
- **WHEN** a classic session-start event with source `clear` crosses the module
- **THEN** the status line is cleared, the pane reads that no settle run is live, and a later settle line sets no status line and is named once on the debug log
- **AND** a `compact` source leaves the line, the groups and the counts unchanged
- **AND** when a spec run is live in the same session as a live settle run, the status line reads the spec line and the settle pane keeps drawing; when the spec run is at its checkpoint and the settle run is live, the status line reads the settle line; and when the settle run is done and the spec run is at its checkpoint, it reads the spec line
- **AND** when a spec run is at its checkpoint and an interlock gate line of the settle run's review crosses, the settle reader files it although the spec reader declines it

### Requirement: The settle meter SHALL observe only, from the pinned lines and the pinned role sources, and the guarantee SHALL be pinned statically

The settle meter's rules SHALL live in one pure module, `lib/settle-meter.mjs`, that imports nothing from `node:`, spells no engine call, and is reached from the hooks module through the pinned Node-free import walk. Every hook the settle meter adds or joins SHALL resolve to the engine's own behaviour: `next(e)`, `yield* next(e)`, a drawing, or an empty command reply; it SHALL add no deny, no substitute result, no catch handler, no new engine call, no new hooked event name, no new session-state key and no timer. A `node --test` case SHALL assert: that the hooks module's engine calls are still the recorded allow-list and its hooked event names the recorded list; that `SETTLE_PANE` is spelled in the hooks module as the pure module exports it; that neither the hooks module, the spec meter's rules nor the settle meter's rules spell the word `complete` or `interlock:advisor`; that the prompt, Skill and Read observers still pass their events on as they came; that `roleOf` classifies the first line of each bundled dimension brief, the first sentence of each of review-code's two skeptic blockquotes, the first line the remediate prompt assembler prints and the first line the conformance brief prints, each as its role, and a delimited repository review policy block followed by a dimension brief as that dimension; that every stage, as the settle reader splits it, of every fenced `interlock`, `gh`, `glab` and `git` command line of the settle skill and every fenced `interlock` line of the review-code skill is keyed, where a stage whose first word is `interlock` SHALL have a kind and only a non-`interlock` stage MAY instead match a command prefix the test writes down; and that every keyed line kind appears in some skill line; and that the kit's settle fixtures are the captured payloads, by provenance. The mod's tests for the settle meter SHALL live under `test/mod/` as `*.test.ts`, run by `claude plugin test`, and never be collected by `npm test`.

#### Scenario: Happy path — the pins hold on the shipped module

- **GIVEN** the module and the pure settle module as shipped
- **WHEN** `node --test test/spine/mod-pins.test.mjs test/spine/settle-meter.test.mjs` runs and then `claude plugin validate . --strict`
- **THEN** the allow-list, the event list, the `SETTLE_PANE` pin, the word pins, the role-source pin, the skill-lines pin and the fixture mirror all pass
- **AND** the validator's `hooks:` line lists the `interlock-settle` pane and its command beside the four earlier panes and commands, and its `calls:` line names nothing the settle meter added

#### Scenario: Failure — a reworded role source or a stray skill line fails a pin

- **GIVEN** the second skeptic blockquote in `skills/review-code/SKILL.md` reworded so its first sentence no longer begins `You are an independent reviewer giving a second opinion.`, or a new fenced `interlock settle <word>` line added to the settle skill that no keyed line covers, or a new `interlock` verb piped after an allowed `git diff` stage, or `lib/settle-meter.mjs` importing `node:path`
- **WHEN** `npm test` runs
- **THEN** the role-source pin, the skill-lines pin or the import walk fails naming the sentence, the line or the import
- **AND** no session needs to load the module to find it

#### Scenario: Edge case — a hook that throws is skipped and the engine's behaviour stands

- **GIVEN** a Bash result that makes the settle line reader throw, a spawn whose prompt is not a string, or a pane draw whose clock read rejects
- **WHEN** the engine runs the chain
- **THEN** the tool call, the spawn or the draw resolves as the engine alone would have resolved it
- **AND** the module's later hooks keep working and one debug-log line names what was not drawn
livingTexts.hooks/spec-meter:
# hooks/spec-meter Specification

## Purpose

Shows an `/interlock:spec` run while it runs: a status line naming the change and the last thing the CLI printed, and a pane with the artifact ladder, the ledger, validate, gate and readiness results by field, the explore fan-out and the writes, drawn by the same hooks module as the ship meter from what crossed the Bash tool and the Write tool, and deciding nothing.

## Requirements

### Requirement: The spec meter SHALL go live only on the plugin's spec skill load in an interactive session, and SHALL take the change name from the CLI alone

The module SHALL start a spec run only when the plugin's spec skill is loaded in a session whose start reported it interactive: a prompt submitted whose first word is `/interlock:spec`, or a Skill tool call naming `interlock:spec` that the engine did not mark errored. The engine raises no skill-prompt event for a plugin skill (probed on Claude Code 2.1.291), so the load is read from these two events as they cross. An `openspec` or `interlock` command crossing the Bash tool SHALL never start one, so a stock OpenSpec flow in the same session draws nothing. The prompt and the Skill call SHALL be passed on exactly as they came, and of the prompt only its first word SHALL be read. At the start the status line and the pane SHALL read `change: unknown until named`; the change name SHALL be taken only from the CLI's own argv (`openspec new change "<name>"`, `--change "<name>"`, the explicit name on `interlock ledger|validate|ready|notify checkpoint "<name>"`, `--metrics <name>`) or from a `changeName` or `change` field in a result's JSON, never from a file path, a prompt or a tool input. The record SHALL keep results per change name; the status line and the pane SHALL follow the name the CLI named last and the pane SHALL list every other name seen in the run. A second spec skill load in the same session SHALL start the record over and say so once on the debug log. In a non-interactive session every hook this requirement adds SHALL return at its first line.

#### Scenario: Happy path — the skill load starts the run and the CLI names the change

- **GIVEN** an interactive session
- **WHEN** the prompt `/interlock:spec add the thing` is submitted
- **THEN** the status line reads `interlock spec: change: unknown until named`, the pane is opened unasked, and the prompt reaches the engine unchanged
- **AND** when a Bash call `openspec new change "add-the-thing"` resolves, the status line reads `interlock spec: add-the-thing · new change` and the pane's header names `add-the-thing`

#### Scenario: Failure — a non-interactive session draws nothing

- **GIVEN** `session.start` reporting `isInteractive: false`
- **WHEN** the prompt `/interlock:spec add the thing` is submitted, or a Skill call names `interlock:spec`, and the same `openspec` and `interlock` lines, writes and spawns follow
- **THEN** no status line is set, no pane is opened, no toast is shown and no record is kept
- **AND** every hook resolved to what the engine alone would have done

#### Scenario: Edge case — a stock OpenSpec flow, a standalone explore, and two active changes

- **GIVEN** an interactive session in which the spec skill was not loaded
- **WHEN** `openspec new change "other"`, `openspec status --change "other" --json` and a Write under `openspec/changes/other/` cross the module, or the plugin's explore skill alone is loaded and spawns three `Explore` agents
- **THEN** no status line is set and the pane reads that no spec run is live in this session
- **AND** in a live spec run where `openspec status --change "alpha" --json` and then `openspec status --change "beta" --json` cross, the status line follows `beta`, the pane draws `beta`'s table and lists `alpha` as another change named this run, and `alpha`'s results are kept under its own name

### Requirement: The status line and the pane SHALL repeat the CLI's own words from the lines it ran, and SHALL make no verdict of their own

While a spec run is live, a Bash call whose command, or one of its segments, begins with one of the flow's keyed lines SHALL be let through and its result read. Segments are split at unquoted `&&`, `||`, `;` or line breaks.

The keyed lines and the fields read from each:
- `openspec new change`
- `openspec status … --json`, for the artifact ladder: `artifacts[].id`, `status`, `requires`, `outputPath` and `applyRequires`; never `isComplete` or `isPlanningComplete`
- `interlock drift --json`: `unarchived`, `stale.broken`, `stale.aging`, by count
- `interlock note match … --json`: `rows` by count, `omitted` and `unreadable`; or `error` with `candidates` when the change did not resolve, read as the ledger and validate lines read it
- `interlock ledger … --json`: `blocking`, `needsHuman`, `invalidCount`, `missing`, `unparseable`
- `interlock validate … --json`: `ready` and `problems`, or `error` with `candidates`
- `interlock gate … --json`: `passed`, `counts`, `malformed`, `metrics.written`, `metrics.reason`
- `interlock autonomy record` and `interlock autonomy clean`: the command tokens only; no level, no count and no text of the result
- `interlock ready … --json`: `ready`, and `blockers` by count
- `interlock notify checkpoint`

The stage on the status line SHALL be composed from those fields in the CLI's words, for example: `status 2/4 done · next: design`, `notes 2 matched (omitted 0)`, `ledger blocking (needs_human 2 · invalid 0)`, `ledger missing`, `validate READY`, `validate NOT READY (problems 2)`, `gate BLOCKED (blocker 1 · warning 3)`, `gate PASS (metrics not written)`, `autonomy record`, `ready false (blockers 2)`, `checkpoint`.

Reading rules:
- Segments SHALL be applied in the command's order.
- A keyed line that reads no result text (`openspec new change`, `interlock autonomy`, `interlock notify checkpoint`) SHALL be applied from any segment by its own argv.
- A keyed line whose result is read SHALL be read only when it is the one such line in the command. Two or more in one command SHALL each be shown as unparsed with the reason `compound command`.
- A result that does not parse as JSON, or that lacks the fields the line names, SHALL be shown as that line with `(unparsed)` and its first line of text on the pane, never as a verdict, and SHALL leave one debug-log line.
- An artifact table whose every artifact is `done` SHALL read `status 4/4 done` and never `complete`.
- Every other Bash call, including any `interlock advisor` line, SHALL be passed through at the first line, its result unread.
- The module SHALL compare no count against any threshold and SHALL show no `quiet <n> min`.

#### Scenario: Happy path — the ladder advances in the CLI's words

- **GIVEN** a live spec run named `add-the-thing`
- **WHEN** these resolve in turn:
  - `openspec status --change "add-the-thing" --json`, with `proposal` and `specs` done, `design` ready and `tasks` blocked
  - `interlock ledger "add-the-thing" --json`, with `blocking: true`, `needsHuman: 2`, `invalidCount: 0`
  - `interlock validate "add-the-thing" --json`, with `ready: true` and no problems
  - `interlock gate --findings … --metrics add-the-thing --json`, with `passed: false` and counts `blocker 1`, `warning 3`, `suggestion 0`
- **THEN** the status line reads, in turn, `interlock spec: add-the-thing · status 2/4 done · next: design`, `… · ledger blocking (needs_human 2 · invalid 0)`, `… · validate READY`, `… · gate BLOCKED (blocker 1 · warning 3)`
- **AND** the pane's artifact table carries four rows with OpenSpec's own status words, and its ledger, validate and gate lines carry the same fields
- **AND** when `interlock note match "add-the-thing" --json` resolves with two `rows`, `omitted: 0` and `unreadable: 1`, the status line reads `… · notes 2 matched (omitted 0)` and the pane's notes line reads `notes: 2 matched · omitted 0 · unreadable 1`

#### Scenario: Failure — a text-only gate line is shown as unparsed, never as a verdict

- **GIVEN** a live spec run, and a consumer repository on the previous skill text whose ledger line is `interlock ledger "add-the-thing"` with no `--json`
- **WHEN** that call resolves with `DECISIONS BLOCKING — 3 row(s): 1 needs_human, 2 agent_resolved, 0 invalid`
- **THEN** the status line reads `interlock spec: add-the-thing · ledger (unparsed)`
- **AND** the pane's ledger line reads `ledger: not read (output not JSON)` with that first line of text beside it, and no `blocking`, `clear`, `pass` or `blocked` word is composed from it
- **AND** one debug-log line names the command and the reason, and the pane's gate line still reads `gate: not run yet`
- **AND** when `interlock note match "add-the-thing" --json` exits non-zero with `interlock: docs/notes/compound.md: header row missing`, the status line reads `… · notes (unparsed)` and the pane's notes line carries that first line of text
- **AND** when a consumer repository on the previous skill text runs `interlock advisor "add-the-thing" --brief --json`, the call passes through unread and neither surface changes

#### Scenario: Edge case — an all-done ladder, a write with no status call, and an autonomy line

- **GIVEN** a live spec run named `add-the-thing`
- **WHEN** `openspec status --change "add-the-thing" --json` resolves with every artifact `done` and `isComplete: true`
- **THEN** the status line reads `interlock spec: add-the-thing · status 4/4 done`, and neither it nor the pane contains the word `complete`
- **AND** when a Write to `openspec/changes/add-the-thing/tasks.md` crosses with no status call after it, the table still shows the statuses the last status call printed and the writes section counts the write
- **AND** when `interlock autonomy record review-artifacts --blockers 1` resolves with `review-artifacts: L1 (0/3 clean)`, the status line reads `… · autonomy record` and no level, count or `clean` word from that text appears anywhere
- **AND** when the one command `openspec new change "add-the-thing" && openspec status --change "add-the-thing" --json` resolves, the table is the status call's
- **AND** when `interlock autonomy clean review-artifacts explore spec; interlock notify checkpoint "add-the-thing"` resolves, the run stops at its checkpoint
- **AND** when `interlock note match "add-the-thin" --json` resolves with `error` and `candidates: ["add-the-thing"]`, the status line reads `… · notes: change not resolved (candidates 1)`, as the ledger and validate lines read the same result

### Requirement: The pane SHALL draw the run on both surfaces by field, count writes and spawns without reading them as validity, and name the record it is not

`/interlock-spec` SHALL open the pane at any width. At the spec skill's load the module SHALL open it unasked. When the engine declines to seat it, one toast SHALL say the meter is available by command, and nothing else is drawn.

The pane SHALL use only elements that draw on the terminal and the Desktop. It SHALL draw, in this order:
- the change (or `unknown until named`) and the schema the last status named
- the artifact table exactly as the last `openspec status … --json` printed it, `id · status · outputPath`, with `applyRequires` named, or `status: not run yet`
- the explore line: `<n> investigators spawned`, from the `agent.spawn` events whose `subagentType` is `Explore` during the run (or that the host reported none), and the brief's path from the last Write under `.claude/handoff/explore-*.md`, or `no brief written yet`
- the drift counts
- the notes line, `notes: <n> matched · omitted <k> · unreadable <u>`, or `not run yet`
- the ledger, validate, gate and readiness lines by field, or `not run yet`
- the autonomy command last run, or `not run yet`
- the advisor-consults line: `advisor consults seen: session <a> · subagents <b>`, where each count is the number of distinct entries named `advisor` in the `serverToolUses` of the `turn.step` events during the run, keyed by entry id. `<a>` counts events with no `agentId` and `<b>` counts events with one. The line is drawn from the run's first such entry onward; before it, the pane has no advisor-consults line
- a writes section listing:
  - each artifact file under `openspec/changes/<name>/` written through the Write or Edit tool, with a count and the last time
  - the findings file's path, from the last Write under `.claude/metrics/review-artifacts-<name>-*.json`
  - no status word beside any of them
- `last activity <ISO>` from the engine's clock, or `last activity unknown`
- one line reading `the artifacts on disk, the findings file and the gate's exit are the record`

Rules:
- A write whose result the engine marked errored SHALL not be counted.
- The advisor-consults count SHALL be drawn and never compared, and its word SHALL be `seen`. The meter does not read settings, so it cannot tell a tool that is off from an engine that never reports server tool uses. Neither SHALL draw a line that reads as a measured zero.
- When no spec run is live, the pane SHALL say so.
- The module SHALL never close the pane itself.
- No pane text SHALL contain the word `complete`.
- A row SHALL carry no colour of the meter's own: a tone SHALL only name what a word the CLI or the engine printed means — an artifact's status word, a field the CLI printed as `true` or `false`, `not run yet` — and SHALL leave the row's text unchanged.

#### Scenario: Happy path — the pane mounts on both surfaces with the table, the counts and the writes

- **GIVEN** a live spec run named `add-the-thing` after:
  - three `Explore` spawns
  - a Write to `.claude/handoff/explore-add-the-thing-20261006-120000.md`
  - one status call
  - two Writes to `openspec/changes/add-the-thing/proposal.md`
  - a Write to `.claude/metrics/review-artifacts-add-the-thing-20261006-121500.json`
  - two `turn.step` events with no `agentId` and one with an `agentId`, whose `serverToolUses` each carry one entry named `advisor`, with distinct ids
- **WHEN** the pane is mounted on `terminal` and then on `desktop`
- **THEN** on each surface these are found by key: the artifact rows, the explore line (`3 investigators spawned`, the brief's path), the writes line for `proposal.md` (`written 2×` with its last time), the findings path, the line `advisor consults seen: session 2 · subagents 1`, and the `last activity` line
- **AND** no row carries a tick, a threshold or the word `complete`, and a row's colour is only a tone naming a word the CLI printed

#### Scenario: Failure — the engine declines the unasked open, and a denied write is not counted

- **GIVEN** a terminal narrower than the engine's floor for an unasked pane
- **WHEN** the spec skill is loaded and the module opens the pane
- **THEN** the open resolves unplaced and exactly one toast says `/interlock-spec opens the spec meter`, and no pane is drawn until the command is typed
- **AND** when a later Write to `openspec/changes/add-the-thing/tasks.md` resolves with `isError: true`, the writes section does not count it
- **AND** when a `turn.step` event repeats an advisor entry id already counted, the advisor-consults line does not change

#### Scenario: Edge case — no run, and a run that has not named its change

- **GIVEN** a session in which the spec skill was not loaded
- **WHEN** `/interlock-spec` is typed
- **THEN** the pane reads that no spec run is live in this session, and nothing else
- **AND** in a live run before any name crossed, the pane's header reads `change: unknown until named`, every result line reads `not run yet`, no advisor-consults line is drawn, and a Write under `openspec/changes/<some-name>/` does not name the change
- **AND** when every `turn.step` event in a live run lacks `serverToolUses`, or carries none named `advisor`, no advisor-consults line is drawn, no pane text contains `none seen`, and no other line changes

### Requirement: The spec pane SHALL be drawn as titled cards with toned words from fields beside unchanged row texts

Each spec pane line SHALL keep the text it reads today. Beside it, each line SHALL carry its section — `header`, `artifacts`, `explore`, `gates`, `writes` or `record` — and coloured spans whose concatenation is exactly the text. At or above the card floor (`wave board min width (columns)` from `interlock limits`), the module SHALL draw the lines as a header card and titled cards, using `borderStyle: 'single'` alone. Below the floor, or with no width reported, it SHALL draw the same lines flat with no border.

Tones:
- An artifact status word: `done` the ok colour, `ready` the current colour, `blocked` dim.
- A field the gate, ledger, validate or readiness line printed as `true` or `false`: the ok colour when the CLI's own field reads it ready, passed or not blocking; the alarm colour otherwise.
- `not run yet`, and the record line: dim.
- A result not read: the warn colour.
- The checkpoint and hand-over lines: the accent colour.

A card's title SHALL be drawn from the line's section and SHALL never be a keyed row. With no spec run live the pane SHALL draw its one no-run text and nothing else, and SHALL add no tick, glyph or word of its own.

#### Scenario: Happy path — a stopped run reads as cards with its gate coloured

- **GIVEN** a spec run at its checkpoint whose status shows four artifacts `done`, whose ledger line printed `blocking false`, whose validate line printed `ready true` and whose gate line printed `passed false`
- **WHEN** the pane is drawn at 120 columns on the terminal and on the desktop
- **THEN** the header card is followed by the cards titled `artifacts`, `explore`, `gates`, `writes` and `record`, each with a single border
- **AND** each `done` takes the ok colour, `blocking false` and `ready true` take the ok colour, `passed false` takes the alarm colour, the checkpoint line takes the accent colour, and every keyed row reads exactly the text it read before this change

#### Scenario: Edge case — a run before any line has crossed

- **GIVEN** a live spec run in which no keyed line has crossed yet
- **WHEN** the pane is drawn
- **THEN** every `not run yet` is dim, the `artifacts` card holds the `status: not run yet` row, and no card is titled for a section with no line
- **AND** the no-run pane, drawn in a session with no spec run, is one text and no card

#### Scenario: Failure — a narrow pane draws flat

- **GIVEN** a live spec run with its status read
- **WHEN** the pane is drawn at 40 columns
- **THEN** no Box has a border, no card title is drawn, and every keyed row still reads its text

### Requirement: The spec run SHALL end at the checkpoint, at an accepted ship launch and at the session boundary, and the module SHALL own one status line

When `interlock notify checkpoint` crosses the module, whatever its result, the run SHALL stop at its checkpoint: the status line SHALL read `interlock spec: <change> · checkpoint` and stay, the pane SHALL keep its last results and add the time the checkpoint crossed, and a later keyed line SHALL change nothing and be named once on the debug log. When a Workflow tool call that the launch rule recognises as a ship launch returns a result the launch rule recognises as accepted, the spec run SHALL end before the ship run becomes live, so the ship meter's status line replaces the spec meter's with no second writer; the readiness result that crossed before the launch SHALL stay on the pane until the boundary. At a classic session-start event whose source is `clear`, `resume` or `fork` the spec run SHALL reset in the same hook and on the same event as the ship run and the settle run, the status line cleared and the pane redrawn to its no-run text; a source of `startup` or `compact` SHALL leave it as it is. The module SHALL compose its one status line in one place, a live run ranking above a finished one: the ship position while a ship run is live, otherwise the spec line while a spec run is live, otherwise the settle line while a settle run is live, otherwise the spec line while a spec run is stopped at its checkpoint, otherwise the settle line while a settle run is done, otherwise nothing.

#### Scenario: Happy path — the checkpoint ends the run and the line says so

- **GIVEN** a live spec run named `add-the-thing` whose last stage was `gate PASS`
- **WHEN** `interlock notify checkpoint "add-the-thing"` resolves with `push: not configured — set INTERLOCK_NTFY_TOPIC`
- **THEN** the status line reads `interlock spec: add-the-thing · checkpoint` and is not cleared, and the pane reads `checkpoint reached <ISO>` with the gate line still `gate PASS`
- **AND** a later `openspec status --change "add-the-thing" --json` changes neither, and one debug-log line names a keyed line that crossed after the checkpoint

#### Scenario: Failure — a ship launch mid-spec hands the line over

- **GIVEN** a live spec run named `add-the-thing` on the continuity path, where `interlock ready "add-the-thing" --findings … --json` resolved with `ready: true`
- **WHEN** a Workflow call naming `workflows/ship.js` returns `status: 'async_launched'` with a run id
- **THEN** the spec run is no longer live, the status line reads the ship meter's `interlock: add-the-thing …` form and never both, and the spec pane reads `ready true` from before the launch with a line saying the run handed over to ship at `<ISO>`
- **AND** when the launch returns an error or a deny, the spec run stays live and its line stays

#### Scenario: Edge case — a clear mid-spec, a compaction, a second spec load on the same change, and a settle run beside it

- **GIVEN** a live spec run with a status line set and a table drawn
- **WHEN** a classic session-start event with source `clear` crosses the module
- **THEN** the status line is cleared, the pane reads that no spec run is live, and a later `openspec status … --json` sets no status line and is named once on the debug log
- **AND** a `compact` source leaves the line, the table and the counts unchanged
- **AND** when the spec skill is loaded again in the same session for a change that already has results, the record starts over with `change: unknown until named`, the earlier results are not kept, and one debug-log line says a new spec run replaced the previous one
- **AND** when a settle run is live in the same session, the status line reads the spec line while the spec run is live, and the settle line while the spec run is at its checkpoint, and never both

### Requirement: The spec meter SHALL observe only, from the pinned lines, and the guarantee SHALL be pinned statically

Every hook the spec meter adds or extends SHALL resolve to the engine's own behaviour: `next(e)`, a drawing, or an empty command reply. It SHALL return no deny, no substitute result, and no rewritten prompt or Skill call. It SHALL call no model, prompt submission, session message, process, network, file read, file write or permission check. Nothing on disk is needed, because it draws only what crossed the Bash tool and the Write tool, and the server tool uses the engine reports on `turn.step`.

The lines it keys on SHALL be the lines the skill suite pins by token for `spec/machine-readable-gate-lines`. A `node --test` case SHALL read the three skill files' fenced command lines and assert that every pinned keyed line is one the pure text module classifies, so the meter and the pins cannot drift apart silently.

The text rules SHALL live in a pure module under `lib/` that imports no `node:` module, reached by the hooks module's import walk. The text rules are: the skill key and the prompt's first word, the line classifier and the segment split, the change-name reader, the field reader, the stage and status texts, the write classifier, and the advisor-entry reader over `serverToolUses`.

The static pins SHALL:
- record no new hooked event and nothing new among the allowed calls
- assert that neither the prompt hook nor the Skill hook builds a text or a result of its own
- keep the one `deny` the launch rule's
- keep every forbidden token
- keep the session-state keys as declared
- assert that neither the hooks module nor the pure module spells `isComplete`, `isPlanningComplete`, the word `complete`, or `interlock:advisor`

`claude plugin validate --strict` SHALL list the Skill tool hook, the spec pane and its command on the `hooks:` line, and no new method on `calls:`.

#### Scenario: Happy path — the recorded hooks and nothing more

- **GIVEN** the module as shipped
- **WHEN** `claude plugin validate . --strict` and `node --test test/spine/mod-pins.test.mjs` run
- **THEN** the `hooks:` line adds `tool.call{tool=Skill}`, `ui.render{component=Pane, requestId=interlock-spec}` and `command.run{command=interlock-spec}` to the lines the preceding changes recorded, and the `calls:` line adds no method
- **AND** the pins pass with `HOOKED_EVENTS` unchanged, `ALLOWED_CALLS` unchanged, one `deny`, and `['interlock.ledger']` as the only state key

#### Scenario: Failure — a forbidden token, a verdict word or an unpinned line fails a pin

- **GIVEN** the module with any of these:
  - `$.fs.read`, `$.process.run` or `.catch(` added for the spec meter
  - `isComplete` or `interlock:advisor` spelled in `lib/spec-meter.mjs` or `hooks/mod.mjs`
  - a second `deny`, or a `{ text }` of its own in the prompt or Skill hook
- **WHEN** `node --test test/spine/mod-pins.test.mjs` and `node --test test/spine/spec-meter.test.mjs` run
- **THEN** a pin fails naming the token or the word
- **AND** a fenced keyed line added to `skills/spec/SKILL.md` and pinned by the skill suite that the classifier does not recognise fails the skill-lines pin naming the line

#### Scenario: Edge case — a hook that throws is skipped and the flow continues

- **GIVEN** a Bash result that makes the field reader throw, a Skill call whose `skill` is not a string, a Write whose `file_path` is missing, or a `turn.step` event whose `serverToolUses` is not an array
- **WHEN** the engine runs the chain
- **THEN** the tool call, the skill load, the write and the request resolve as the engine alone would have resolved them
- **AND** the module's later hooks keep working and the run record is as it was before the throw
